root_cause: The unCheckAllInputsExcept method filters checkboxes by name attribute instead of the exclusive group attribute, so the exclusive 'No, I do not have any of these symptoms' checkbox fails to uncheck other symptom checkboxes that have distinct names.
repair_strategy: Modify unCheckAllInputsExcept to select checkboxes by the data-checkbox-exclusive-group attribute when present, falling back to name-based selection for backward compatibility, then uncheck matching inputs in the same form except the clicked one.
expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users will now see that checking 'No, I do not have any of these symptoms' clears any previously selected symptom checkboxes, ensuring mutually exclusive selection as intended, improving form correctness and accessibility of exclusive choice.
functional_risks: Changing the selection logic could affect implementations that rely on the name-based behavior for exclusive checkboxes without a group attribute; however the fallback preserves existing behavior.
Risk of inadvertently unchecking checkboxes outside the intended form if forms are misconfigured, but the sameFormOwner check mitigates this.
verification_requirements: After the change, the journey step 5 (tick no symptoms after cough and fever) should result in symptoms[cough] and symptoms[fever] being unchecked (value []).
The exclusive none checkbox should still function when clicked alone (should check itself and leave others unchecked).
Clicking a symptom checkbox should still uncheck the exclusive none checkbox if it is checked (optional but verify).
Ensure that checkboxes without data-checkbox-exclusive-group continue to work as before (if any).
No regression in the conditional reveal functionality (aria-controls) unrelated to exclusive behavior.
